name: Lionel Scaloni

spellsCounted.reason: Proposed by the caller as the single counted spell: interim from August 2018, made permanent later; Copa America 2021, Finalissima 2022, World Cup 2022, Copa America 2024, World Cup 2026 runner-up. Contract runs to December 2026; renewal to 2030 reported but not officially confirmed (2026-10-21).

spellsExcluded.reason: Assistant, not head coach (to Sampaoli's staff period); date not verified in this run.

spellsExcluded.club: Argentina senior team under Jorge Sampaoli (assistant)
spellsExcluded.reason: Assistant to Sampaoli, including the 2018 World Cup; not head coach. Dates not verified in this run.

scopeNote: Lionel Scaloni's only head-coach job: Argentina national team, 2018-08-02 (beIN Sports; interim after Sampaoli) to ongoing as of 2026-11-04. Counted period covers the whole spell, but the best-documented sub-periods are the 2021 Copa America (Coaches' Voice, 4-4-2/4-3-3 with Messi and Lautaro up front), the 2022 World Cup knockouts (shape shuffled per opponent: 4-3-3, 3-5-2, four-man midfield vs Croatia; man-oriented matchups in the final) and, thinly, 2025 (4-1-4-1 / 4-3-1-2 per MBP School) and the 2026 World Cup (mostly press quotes, no tier A-B tactical study found). The 2018-2020 and 2024 Copa America periods have almost no tactical coverage in what was read. Style term used by sources: flexible, 'pragmatismo camaleonico' (Perfil), not a fixed system; Coaches' Voice describes man-oriented 1v1 defending from the lower block (compared with Bielsa) with zonal elements only on corners. Player-empowerment evidence: Messi given freedom to drift (Coaches' Voice), squad chosen to let him play (FIFA interview), Di Maria excused from defending in the 2022 final, but Scaloni explicitly denies that Messi picks the team (June 2026). Several search-result pages (Lazada, FM sites, Sofascore) were SEO or unreadable and not used. Coaches' Voice article date is guessed by the miner (2022-02-18); the content refers to 2021. 2026 World Cup: Argentina lost the final 1-0 a.e.t. to Spain on 2026-07-19 (Teletica).
openQuestions: Date Scaloni was made permanent (after interim from 2018-08-02): not verified; beIN says the AFA ratified him but gives no date.

Contract renewal to 2030 (reported 2026-10-21 by Noticias NQN and others) is not officially confirmed by AFA; current deal ends December 2026. Teletica says a verbal agreement was reported before the final, while Scaloni said after the final he would honour the contract and then decide.
Shape in the 2022 final: sources disagree (4-4-2 vs 3-5-2); no tier A-B source read for it.

Contested label: Perfil and Yahoo describe pragmatic flexibility; Coaches' Voice describes a consistent 4-4-2 with high press and patient build-up. Whether Messi shapes the lineup is contradictory (Olé interview 'every decision spoken with him' per search summary vs Scaloni's 2026 denial).
The 2024 Copa America and the 2026 World Cup have no tier A-B tactical analysis in this file.
Assistant jobs (U-20, Sampaoli) dates not verified.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Scaloni's first teams featured a back four that, through featuring a player of the nature of Juan Foyth at right-back, gave them the flexibility to build with a back three. Doing so meant that width was sacrificed on the right; Nicolás Tagliafico overlapped from left-back and around the narrow midfield that existed in either a 4-4-2 (below), 4-3-3 or four-diamond-two

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: regardless of their defensive approach, a 4-4-2 is retained.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: They have consistently sought to build patiently and dominate possession. Their central defenders split and a central midfielder withdraws to, with their goalkeeper, form a diamond around the opposition's most advanced pressers, when there exists the versatility to build around pressure, often via direct passes to their full-backs

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Central combinations have consistently been influential in Argentina's attacks under Scaloni, and some have evolved from their efficient high press.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Scaloni favours an aggressive press that is applied upon losses of possession and that involves his team defending well into the attacking half of the pitch. They have also demonstrated a desire to force possession wide when regains are unlikely, or when their high press is unlikely to succeed.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: When their high press is being applied (above), the wider midfielders in Argentina's 4-4-2 support their front two in pressing their opposing back four. That same front two initially screens access into the opposing defensive midfielders before moving to instead take the relevant central defenders

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: On the occasions they are defending with a lower block (above), aggressive pressure continues to be applied through the centre of the pitch to attempt to force the ball wide, in the knowledge that their two lines of four are effective at defending against any crosses likely to follow. Further forwards, Messi and Martínez remain advanced and positioned away from opposing defensive midfielders, and ultimately braced to launch potential counters. From that lower block Argentina's priority in wide territory becomes one-on-ones, which means that, not unlike the approach overseen by Marcelo Bielsa, players are mostly responsible for their direct opponent.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: It is when a 4-3-3 proves Scaloni's preference that a mid-block (above) is likeliest to be used, even if from that 4-3-3 there are still moments when they defend with a 4-4-2 via one of their front three withdrawing into midfield

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: The existence of two central midfielders provides them with the reliable transitional foundation they require

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Further forwards, Messi and Martínez remain advanced and positioned away from opposing defensive midfielders, and ultimately braced to launch potential counters.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: When González is on the left, Argentina's right-sided midfielder instead moves infield, in turn encouraging Messi to drift wide (above) and therefore to receive and create from outside of their opponent's defensive block while supported by their right-back.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: their full-backs provide their attacking width, and Messi operates as a playmaker from a central position (below).

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: When defending corners, three players form a staggered zonal defence, and the others defend one-on-one.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Set-pieces have proved a further strength. Messi poses a threat from direct free kicks, and, in addition to Messi, Paredes and De Paul provide variety from corners and wider deliveries. Five players occupy the penalty area at those set-pieces

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Regardless of how far an opposing full-back may venture, the wide midfielder opposite him is responsible for tracking his run.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Lautaro Martínez and Messi from Scaloni's favoured front two. Martínez mostly remains advanced and works to discourage opposing defenders from advancing, and Messi is given significant freedom to contribute from deeper territory when attacks are being built

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: To that end, Scaloni has increasingly favoured versatile wide midfielders, instead of relying on his talented attackers to defend at key moments.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni: Coach Watch - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: "It is a huge title, especially for our people; I hope that the Argentines enjoy it," he said of their Copa America triumph over rivals Brazil. "The fans support the team unconditionally. They can identify with this team that never gives up."

sources.title: How Argentina outmanoeuvred Croatia's magic midfield to reach the World Cup final
sources.evidence: For the third time in as many knockout games, Lionel Scaloni shuffled his system, altered his defensive approach and ensured Argentina had the tools to win a game at the World Cup 2022.

sources.title: How Argentina outmanoeuvred Croatia's magic midfield to reach the World Cup final
sources.evidence: From the 4-3-3 against Australia, to the 3-5-2 against the Dutch, here it was very much a four-man midfield picked in place to thwart, frustrate and eventually get beyond the dominant Croatia midfield.

sources.title: How Argentina outmanoeuvred Croatia's magic midfield to reach the World Cup final
sources.evidence: It wasn't an outright aggressive press, nor even an attempt to directly challenge for the ball every single time, but rather to control the space in which the game was played.

sources.title: How Argentina outmanoeuvred Croatia's magic midfield to reach the World Cup final
sources.evidence: Any time the Croatia middle three took possession, an immediate shuttle run was required by one of the Argentina four: make it a two-versus-one every time. Cut off the passing lane, force a backwards turn or sideways ball.

sources.title: How Argentina outmanoeuvred Croatia's magic midfield to reach the World Cup final
sources.evidence: Mac Allister drifted from the left into a more advanced and often central role, the link between midfield and attack, with Enzo always happy to dovetail with him in turn.

sources.title: How Argentina outmanoeuvred Croatia's magic midfield to reach the World Cup final
sources.evidence: It's not even necessarily tactical brilliance from the head coach, but rather an innate appreciation of which of his players can perform the roles he wants against each opponent

sources.title: How Argentina outmanoeuvred Croatia's magic midfield to reach the World Cup final
sources.evidence: Scaloni has shown admirable insight and earned all-important buy-in.

sources.title: How Argentina outmanoeuvred Croatia's magic midfield to reach the World Cup final
sources.evidence: Messi out of possession was in his usual walking mode, but narrow, simply stopping the easy ball.

sources.title: Tagliafico and Molina: The Full-Backs of Scaloni's Argentina National Team - MBP School of coaches
sources.evidence: Argentina, under the guidance of Lionel Scaloni, has primarily used a 4-3-1-2 formation. However, in their most recent match against Brazil — which we'll focus on — Scaloni opted for a 4-1-4-1 setup.

sources.title: Tagliafico and Molina: The Full-Backs of Scaloni's Argentina National Team - MBP School of coaches
sources.evidence: In this tactical structure, the coach chose not to use traditional wingers. Instead, it was the full-backs, Tagliafico and Molina, who were responsible for providing width and depth in attack.

sources.title: Tagliafico and Molina: The Full-Backs of Scaloni's Argentina National Team - MBP School of coaches
sources.evidence: This approach caused the opposing full-backs — in this case, Wesley and Arana — to lack clear marking references. Argentina's attacking midfielders occupied the central areas, creating confusion within Brazil's defensive line

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni reveals the 'secret tactics' to win the 2022 World Cup final against France
sources.evidence: So, number by number, he picked the matchups for the final. For example, Nicolas Otamendi with Olivier Giroud, Alexis Mac Allister taking Antoine Griezmann or a two-player system of Nahuel Molina and Cristian Romero to 'eliminate' the threat of Kylian Mbappe.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni reveals the 'secret tactics' to win the 2022 World Cup final against France
sources.evidence: The idea was to prevent him of getting the ball looking forward. As fast as he is, if he's playing backward, we immediately had to pressure him because he had to turn around.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni reveals the 'secret tactics' to win the 2022 World Cup final against France
sources.evidence: We wanted to avoid Di Maria coming back to defend Dembele. First, because defending it's not his thing and then because he had to be fresh to attack constantly (Jules) Kounde.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni reveals the 'secret tactics' to win the 2022 World Cup final against France
sources.evidence: Lionel Scaloni only used numbers to translate the message for his players. "My handwriting is ugly. That's why I like to explain it with numbers."

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni speaks on Argentina penalty kicks, Lionel Messi, World Cup
sources.evidence: We believe strongly in recovering the ball within the first three, four or five seconds after losing possession. If we can't win the ball back, we move into midfield and wait. We never suffered many counter-attacks due to our team's [defensive] work and keeping the opposition wingers in check.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni speaks on Argentina penalty kicks, Lionel Messi, World Cup
sources.evidence: In the first few months with the national team we tried to play a bit faster, a bit more direct and noticed he wasn't comfortable and his teammates weren't comfortable, so I think one of our merits, of all of us, the squad as a whole, was having found those players who could let him play his football.

sources.title: Lionel Scaloni speaks on Argentina penalty kicks, Lionel Messi, World Cup
sources.evidence: having found those players who could let him play his football.

sources.title: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni comments on the team, Lionel Messi, Angel Di Maria, tactics (TyC Sports interview)
sources.evidence: With me, Leo will always play and when he doesn't, it's because I don't see him in the best conditions. In that, we have no problem. It's obvious that there are moments but everything is spoken about. I'm of the idea that he always has to be there, he is untouchable. We respect ourselves and that is the most important.

sources.title: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni comments on the team, Lionel Messi, Angel Di Maria, tactics (TyC Sports interview)
sources.evidence: You cannot always play the same way and with the same players. They understand that the team did not lose its essence. The level is very even, it would be very unfair to say that I have a starting eleven. I respect those who don't understand it but it has to be. Today, only Messi is for sure.

sources.title: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni comments on the team, Lionel Messi, Angel Di Maria, tactics (TyC Sports interview)
sources.evidence: It interests me that everyone trains hard and thinking that anyone can play. I think that not every match is the same. In some, you may need a different type of a winger or a different midfield.

sources.title: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni comments on the team, Lionel Messi, Angel Di Maria, tactics (TyC Sports interview)
sources.evidence: When the 2018 World Cup finished, I had a relation with most of the players and what I told him was that he didn't have to step down from the Argentina national team. Many decided to publicly announce that they would not be continuing.

sources.title: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni comments on the team, Lionel Messi, Angel Di Maria, tactics (TyC Sports interview)
sources.evidence: At some point, I thought I had to go to the bench against Paraguay but I decided to let him play. To risk a player for 35 minutes, I prefer to take him out from the start.

sources.title: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni comments on the team, Lionel Messi, Angel Di Maria, tactics (TyC Sports interview)
sources.evidence: The important thing is that he feels important and to have that feeling of freedom of being able to go to the pitch, do a nutmeg or a dribble, something that does greatly.

sources.title: Scaloni desmintió que Messi arme el equipo y apuntó contra un medio extranjero: "Me jodió"
sources.evidence: Si bien reconoció que mantiene diálogo permanente con Messi y que considera su opinión, dejó en claro que la responsabilidad de definir el once titular y el funcionamiento del equipo recae exclusivamente sobre el cuerpo técnico. "No voy a hacer nada que él no quiera y no tengo problema en decirlo. Ahora, a partir de ahí decido yo cómo juega el equipo"

sources.title: Scaloni desmintió que Messi arme el equipo y apuntó contra un medio extranjero: "Me jodió"
sources.evidence: "Un medio de afuera tergiversó la respuesta. No es cierto. Él trabaja de la misma manera que yo. El equipo lo arma el DT"

sources.title: Scaloni desmintió que Messi arme el equipo y apuntó contra un medio extranjero: "Me jodió"
sources.evidence: "En los años que llevo acá nunca dijo una palabra del equipo"

sources.title: 'Imagine telling Lionel Messi to pass' - Scaloni ... 'remote-controlled' modern football tactics | Goal.com
sources.evidence: Imagine if Messi when he was eight years old had been told all the time 'Pass it!' by his coaches, we wouldn't have him today. ... Let him play ball, let him make mistakes, and when he's 14 or 15 we'll start correcting him.

sources.title: How Did Lionel Scaloni Build the Argentine National Team Around Lionel Messi? (beIN Sports)
sources.evidence: Lionel Scaloni took over the Argentine National Team on August 2, 2018, following the departure of Jorge Sampaoli and the blow that the World Cup in Russia represented. Initially, his role was interim, but he quickly proved that he could lead a generational change.

sources.title: How Did Lionel Scaloni Build the Argentine National Team Around Lionel Messi? (beIN Sports)
sources.evidence: The first step of Scaloni was to bring back Lionel Messi, who had been going through difficult times with the national team. He got him back and then surrounded the captain with young players willing to play for him.

sources.title: How Did Lionel Scaloni Build the Argentine National Team Around Lionel Messi? (beIN Sports)
sources.evidence: That locker room became a space of admiration and commitment, where the footballers repeated: "We play for Messi."

sources.title: Messi, Scaloni and the arduous reconstruction of 'La Selección' (Buenos Aires Times)
sources.evidence: Scaloni drew together a coaching staff full of other heavy-hitting ex-national team players including Pablo "the Clown" Aimar, Walter "the Wall" Samuel and Roberto "the Mouse" Ayala. ... They rejuvenated the squad that many contemptuously called Messi's "group of buddies," and brought along a generation of younger, unknown players.

sources.title: Messi, Scaloni and the arduous reconstruction of 'La Selección' (Buenos Aires Times)
sources.evidence: Scaloni realised he needed to renovate his team once again, brought in a few youngsters, changed the shape, and found the answers he needed.

sources.title: Messi, Scaloni and the arduous reconstruction of 'La Selección' (Buenos Aires Times)
sources.evidence: Messi was surrounded by a team that relied on him, but also helped out, in particular in high pressure situations. ... defensively solid, conceding only three goals in the whole tournament.

sources.title: Messi, Scaloni and the arduous reconstruction of 'La Selección' (Buenos Aires Times)
sources.evidence: Scaloni found a midpoint between playing beautiful football and doing anything to win, sometimes taking control of possession, at others giving the ball to the other team.

sources.title: Scaloni contó sus secretos para manejar el plantel de la Selección: "Es importante hablar" (La Gaceta)
sources.evidence: "Creo que es importante hablar con el jugador, explicarle la situación, de por qué hemos tomado esa decisión, o por qué no juega, aunque en el momento el jugador a lo mejor no lo entiende. Es lógico, pero después recapacita y se da cuenta de que uno actúa en base a lo que siente y que siempre va a ser por el bien común"

sources.title: Scaloni destacó a los suplentes tras la remontada ante Egipto (La Gaceta)
sources.evidence: "El banco también juega" ... "Si no tenés a Lautaro Martínez en el banco, si no tenés a González que corre como un animal y llega, ¿qué entrenador tenés? Podés ser mago, pero lo importante es tener jugadores, esa es la realidad"

sources.title: Scaloni destacó a los suplentes tras la remontada ante Egipto (La Gaceta)
sources.evidence: el técnico sostuvo que la reacción del equipo fue posible gracias al impacto que tuvieron los cambios en un partido que parecía complicarse con el paso de los minutos.

sources.title: Scaloni elogia a Almada y explica por qué reemplazó a Messi ante Colombia (Soccerway ES)
sources.evidence: "al principio no iba a salir, pero cuando él ve que se movían los suplentes y estábamos haciendo dos cambios, me dice que es mejor que salga y lo saqué, sino no salía. Ustedes ya saben cómo funciona (la decisión de dejar o no a Messi en el campo) y qué es lo que pienso"

sources.evidence: "La Selección es lo máximo para cualquier futbolista e hincha. No hay grietas. Cuando logramos tener una conexión 100% somos difíciles de batir."
